subtitle: Invisible Waves, Living Pulses: Jagadish Chandra Bose Between Matter and Life

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot in dim laboratory, Bose framed between a brass wave apparatus and a potted plant
panels.action: Jagadish Chandra Bose stands in his Calcutta lab, one hand on a gleaming horn antenna, the other resting near a delicate plant on a mechanical stand, eyes intent in the half-light.

dialogue.text: In colonial Calcutta, Jagadish Chandra Bose sends invisible electric waves through walls, then turns to ask: do plants feel the secret shocks of the world?

i18n.hi: औपनिवेशिक कलकत्ता में जगदीश चंद्र बोस दीवारों के पार अदृश्य बिजली तरंगें भेजता है, फिर पूछता है: क्या पौधे भी दुनिया के गुप्त झटके महसूस करते हैं?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Bose’s thoughtful face in a crowded Presidency College classroom
panels.action: Jagadish Chandra Bose, in a simple coat, stands before rows of wooden benches at Presidency College, chalk dust on his fingers, listening as a British official reads out staff salaries.

dialogue.text: At Presidency College in the 1890s, Bose hears what every Indian teacher knows: for the same work, an Indian mind earns less than a European one.

i18n.hi: १८९० के दशक में प्रेसिडेंसी कॉलेज में बोस वही सुनता है जो हर भारतीय शिक्षक जानता है: एक ही काम पर भारतीय दिमाग को यूरोपीय से कम मेहनताना मिलता है।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on Bose’s clenched hand over a rejection letter
panels.action: In a modest office, Bose sits at a wooden desk, a document stating reduced pay before him, his hand resting firmly on it, face calm but resolved.

dialogue.speaker: jagadish_chandra_bose
dialogue.text: Then keep your money. I will not sell science cheaper because I am Indian.

i18n.hi: तो अपना पैसा रखो। मैं भारतीय हूँ, इसलिए विज्ञान सस्ता नहीं बेचूँगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a cramped physics laboratory cluttered with handmade apparatus
panels.action: Within a crowded Calcutta physics lab, Bose bends over improvised equipment—battered coils, glass jars, and metal pieces—students watching as he adjusts a small brass screw.

dialogue.text: Refusing reduced pay, Bose keeps working. Instead of bitterness, he turns his anger into delicate instruments, built in a cramped Calcutta lab.

i18n.hi: कम तनख्वाह ठुकराकर बोस काम करता रहता है। कड़वाहट में डूबने के बजाय, वह गुस्से को बारीक औज़ारों में ढालता है, तंग कलकत्ता लैब में।

panels.shot: dramatic side view of Bose aligning a polished brass horn antenna toward a brick wall
panels.action: Bose stands beside a polished horn-shaped antenna and a short metal waveguide tube, carefully aiming the assembly at a solid brick wall inside the lab.

dialogue.text: He chooses a strange frontier: electric waves so short they slip like needles through cracks of matter. Millimetre waves, invisible and sharp.

i18n.hi: वह अजीब सीमा चुनता है: इतनी छोटी बिजली तरंगें जो सुई की तरह पदार्थ की दरारों से फिसल जाएँ। मिलीमीटर तरंगें, अदृश्य और नुकीली।

panels.shot: close-up of Bose’s hands adjusting a tiny crystal detector on a delicate stand
panels.action: His fingers delicately press a slender wire onto a small mineral crystal mounted in a brass frame, an intricate mechanical scale poised to register any faint signal.

dialogue.text: To catch them, he builds a tiny crystal detector, a bit of galena pressed with a fine wire, turning mineral into ear for the unseen.

i18n.hi: उन्हें पकड़ने को वह नन्हा क्रिस्टल डिटेक्टर बनाता है—गैलेना पर महीन तार दबा कर, पत्थर को अनदेखे का कान बना देता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a live demonstration, apparatus on one side of a wall, audience on the other
panels.action: In a colonial hall, dignitaries and students stand around a table; on the far side of a brick wall, Bose’s transmitter glows, while on their side a receiving horn and detector sit ready.

dialogue.text: In Calcutta, he arranges a daring test. Transmitter here, detector there, a heavy wall between. Can waves, unseen, leap stone?

i18n.hi: कलकत्ता में वह साहसी प्रयोग सजाता है। इधर ट्रांसमीटर, उधर डिटेक्टर, बीच में मोटी दीवार। क्या अदृश्य तरंगें पत्थर पर छलाँग लगा सकती हैं?

panels.shot: tight shot on a mechanical indicator just beginning to move as Bose watches
panels.action: Bose leans in, eyes narrowed, as a slim pointer attached to his detector shivers and slowly deflects, while on the other side a student switches the transmitter.

dialogue.text: The transmitter flickers to life. For a breath, nothing. Then the needle trembles. The wall has failed; the waves have passed.

i18n.hi: ट्रांसमीटर झिलमिलाता है। एक सांस तक कुछ नहीं। फिर सुई काँपती है। दीवार हार गई है; तरंगें पार जा चुकी हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bose explaining diagrams of wave polarization to attentive listeners
panels.action: Bose stands beside a blackboard crowded with simple wave diagrams, holding a small crystal between his fingers as European and Indian colleagues listen carefully.

dialogue.text: He publishes in London on electric rays and crystals, showing how these waves bend, polarise, and obey laws like light, yet belong to a different realm.

i18n.hi: लंदन में वह बिजली किरणों और क्रिस्टलों पर छापता है, दिखाता है कैसे ये तरंगें झुकती हैं, ध्रुवित होती हैं, और रोशनी जैसी क़ानून मानती हैं, फिर भी अलग दुनिया की हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Bose looking out a window from his lab toward the bustling streets
panels.action: Alone in his lab at dusk, Bose stands by an open window, instruments behind him, watching the crowded Calcutta street where people move beneath trees and plants.

dialogue.text: But his curiosity is restless. If cold crystals can feel electric waves, what of the warm, green world outside his window?

i18n.hi: पर उसकी जिज्ञासा बेचैन है। अगर ठंडे क्रिस्टल बिजली तरंगें महसूस कर सकते हैं, तो खिड़की के बाहर की गर्म, हरी दुनिया का क्या?

panels.shot: close-up of Bose gently touching a plant placed on a mechanical contrivance
panels.action: He delicately straightens the stem of a small potted plant fixed to a complex brass and glass apparatus, his touch precise, his expression almost reverent.

dialogue.speaker: jagadish_chandra_bose
dialogue.text: If a plant is alive, its pain and joy must leave a trace.

i18n.hi: अगर पौधा ज़िंदा है, तो उसके दर्द और खुशी का कोई निशान ज़रूर होगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of early crescograph setup beside older wave instruments
panels.action: In the same lab, on one table lie the horn antennas and coils; on another, a tall, intricate crescograph rises above a plant, gears and levers poised to magnify its tiniest motions.

dialogue.text: He builds the crescograph, a mechanical magnifier of life. Under its lenses, tiny growths and responses swell into visible lines and curves.

i18n.hi: वह क्रेस्कोग्राफ बनाता है, जीवन का यांत्रिक आवर्धक। इसके नीचे छोटी बढ़त और हलचलें फूली हुई रेखाओं और वक्रों में दिखने लगती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a recording drum tracing a slowly rising line as Bose adjusts a stimulus
panels.action: A smoked glass drum rotates as a fine stylus, driven by the plant’s movement, draws a slowly rising curve; Bose adjusts a controlled stimulus device nearby.

dialogue.text: He applies heat, chemicals, electric shocks, then watches the pen move. The plant does not scream, yet its line jumps like a startled pulse.

i18n.hi: वह गर्मी, रसायन, बिजली के झटके देता है, फिर कलम को देखता है। पौधा चीखता नहीं, पर उसकी रेखा चौंकी नब्ज़ की तरह उछलती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bose presenting his plant-response curves to an audience of scientists
panels.action: In a lecture hall, Bose stands by large charts showing graceful curves of plant response, as European and Indian scientists in formal dress lean forward in curiosity and doubt.

dialogue.text: Abroad, some laugh at ‘sensitive plants’ and Indian mysticism. Bose answers not with poetry, but with graphs, numbers, and meticulous controls.

i18n.hi: विदेश में कुछ लोग ‘संवेदनशील पौधों’ और भारतीय रहस्यवाद पर हँसते हैं। बोस जवाब देता है कविता से नहीं, ग्राफ, आँकड़ों और सख्त परीक्षणों से।

panels.shot: close-up on Bose’s face under lecture hall gaslight, eyes steady as he speaks
panels.action: Under gas lamps, Bose addresses the audience, his face lit from below, calm but intense, one hand resting on the lectern.

dialogue.speaker: jagadish_chandra_bose
dialogue.text: The boundary between living and non-living is not a wall, but a slope.

i18n.hi: जीवित और निर्जीव के बीच की सीमा दीवार नहीं, ढलान है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the foundations of Bose Institute being laid in Calcutta
panels.action: Workers lay stones and raise scaffolding on a new building site, while Bose stands to one side with rolled plans in hand, watching the future laboratory take shape.

dialogue.text: By 1917, he gathers his worlds—waves, crystals, plants—into a single home in Calcutta: the Bose Institute, dedicated to pure inquiry.

i18n.hi: १९१७ तक वह अपनी तीन दुनियाएँ—तरंगें, क्रिस्टल, पौधे—को कलकत्ता में एक घर में समेटता है: बोस संस्थान, शुद्ध खोज को समर्पित।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Bose working at a desk surrounded by both physics and plant instruments
panels.action: Inside the finished institute, Bose writes at a wooden desk, physics apparatus on one side, crescographs and plants on the other, light filtering through high windows.

dialogue.text: He leaves the race to sell wireless telegraphy to others. His prize is different: a deeper map of how matter, living and dead, responds to the world.

i18n.hi: वह वायरलेस टेलीग्राफी बेचने की दौड़ दूसरों पर छोड़ देता है। उसका इनाम अलग है: यह गहरी नक्शा कि जीवित और मृत पदार्थ दुनिया की प्रतिक्रिया कैसे देते हैं।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot: modern scientists examining Bose’s preserved instruments in the institute
panels.action: Decades later, modern researchers walk through a preserved lab room, peering at Bose’s horn antenna, crystal detector, and crescograph displayed in glass cases.

dialogue.text: Long after, engineers trace microwaves and semiconductors back to his tiny crystal, and biophysicists find kinship in his patient plants.

i18n.hi: काफी बाद में इंजीनियर माइक्रोवेव और सेमीकंडक्टरों की जड़ें उसके नन्हे क्रिस्टल तक पहुँचाते हैं, और जैवभौतिकी वाले उसकी धीरज भरी पौधों में अपना भाईपन देखते हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of Bose in his lab doorway, waves apparatus and plants behind him, Calcutta beyond
panels.action: Bose stands silhouetted in the doorway of his institute, behind him the shapes of antennas and crescographs, before him the living city with its trees and people.

dialogue.text: Jagadish Chandra Bose shows that curiosity need not stop at walls—of stone, of discipline, or of life itself. It can pass through, if we build the instruments to listen.

i18n.hi: जगदीश चंद्र बोस दिखाता है कि जिज्ञासा दीवारों पर नहीं रुकती—पत्थर की, विद्या की, या खुद जीवन की। वह पार जा सकती है, बस हमें सुनने वाले औज़ार बनाने हों।

title_i18n.en: Bose Sends Invisible Waves Through Walls
title_i18n.hi: बोस दीवारों के आर-पार अदृश्य तरंगें भेजता है

subtitle_i18n.en: Invisible Waves, Living Pulses: Jagadish Chandra Bose Between Matter and Life
subtitle_i18n.hi: अदृश्य तरंगें, धड़कती लहरें: जगदीश चंद्र बोस, पदार्थ और जीवन के बीच
